summary: CHIRON addresses primary health challenges faced by astronauts during long-duration space missions. Using sensors embedded in the astronaut's suit and connected to the spacecraft’s internal wiring, the system monitors vital signs and provides periodic well-being updates. If irregularities occur, a voice assistant alerts the entire crew and offers actionable guidance. Additionally, an integrated helmet interface called "EVA" ensures continuous health tracking even outside the spacecraft. Periodic monitoring is critical because space triggers unpredictable physiological shifts, such as bone density loss and fluid redistribution. A notable precedent is NASA's "Fist in the Thigh" project, developed to prevent bodily fluids from migrating toward the brain and damaging the ocular region.
details:
Greetings,

Our project represents an innovation upon the health monitoring systems already developed by NASA. It functions primarily by collecting health-related data, including: blood pressure, heart rate, blood sugar, body temperature, sleep duration, mood, oxygen saturation, exercise duration, hydration levels, body mass, stress and fatigue, ambient CO2 and temperature, and cumulative radiation exposure.

This data is gathered through two methods:

"Continuous-wear sensors," which remain with the astronaut at all times.

"Check-up sensors," which the astronaut uses manually.

The data is displayed on a dashboard screen within the spacecraft. This same screen also shows alerts regarding any health anomalies. Additionally, the interface includes an AI-powered chat feature that allows users to ask questions about their health.

This AI is not limited to the dashboard; it also functions as a voice assistant integrated into the spacecraft’s system, providing instructions on how to respond if the alert system detects an anomaly.

Our system would help better safeguard the lives of astronauts during future missions.

For this project, we utilized the following tools: Figma for design; Antigravity for prototype simulation; HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for development; as well as Gemini, YouTube, Google, Claude AI, and DaVinci Resolve.
